content.heading: A language for the work ahead.
content.body: A general-purpose programming language and toolchain built around one challenge: make useful software easier to write, understand, run, and deliver.

content.heading: Libraries and packages
content.body: Python has hundreds of thousands of packages and decades of libraries behind it. Guion ships 27 standard-library modules and a package manager that installs from a local path, a checksummed URL or the Guion package registry, whose log is signed and checked on install. The registry is live, and its first package is frames, a data-frame library.
content.caption: Libraries and packages
content.note: The standard-library modules are listed in the language reference.

content.heading: Arrays and data science
content.body: NumPy and pandas make Python the default for numeric and data work. Guion now has native arrays and a first-party data-frame library, frames, but both are young. In the project's reports on one Mac, the frames workloads took several times as long as pandas from reading a large CSV to the result, and Guion's array compute was still slower than NumPy's.
content.caption: Arrays and data science
content.note: Earlier tests that reached NumPy through Python are retired and no longer cited. The array and data frame reports are in the repository's status page.

content.heading: A release you can use
content.body: Guion 0.2.0 is the first release that is not a preview, for Linux (Debian 12 on ARM64 and x86_64) and macOS on Apple Silicon. It has a written stability policy, a live package registry and native arrays. The Mac build is signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens without a warning; the first launch checks with Apple and needs an internet connection. Guion is still pre-1.0, and Python is a released language with a long track record.

content.heading: Beyond the tasks measured
content.body: Every number on this page is for a named program on a named machine against a named Python version. The server results come from one run on each of two cloud machines; an Intel Xeon server measured Guion slower on an earlier build and has not been rerun. Free-threaded Python and PyPy were not compared.
content.caption: Beyond the tasks measured
content.note: Overall competitiveness remains open, in the project's own words.
